The test image shows a soybean **stem** with brown discoloration on one end transitioning to green, with small specks visible on the surface. Let me check stem disease candidates.

Top candidates based on symptoms: Charcoal_Rot (microsclerotia), Phytophthora (brown stem discoloration), White_Mold (white mold + sclerotia), Anthracnose (dark lesions + fruiting bodies), Rhizoctonia (sunken lesions). Let me view references one at a time.
Charcoal rot reference shows gray stem with peeling epidermis. Similar but not quite matching the specks in the test image. Let me check Phytophthora.
Phytophthora shows whole plant context with brown stems from soil line. Different presentation. Let me check White_Mold.
White mold shows bleached stem with fluffy white mycelium. Different from the test image. Let me check Anthracnose.
Anthracnose shows dark brown/black stems with scattered dark fruiting bodies. Let me check Rhizoctonia.
Rhizoctonia shows sunken lesions at soil line on young green stems. Different context. Let me check Fusarium and Tobacco_Streak_Virus.
Fusarium shows split stems with internal discoloration. Not matching. Let me check Tobacco_Streak_Virus.
Now let me revisit Charcoal_Rot with a second reference to confirm. The test image shows small specks on stem surface consistent with microsclerotia.

This second Charcoal Rot reference is a strong match. The small dark specks (microsclerotia) scattered beneath the epidermis giving a "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance are clearly visible, matching the test image's specked stem surface pattern. The gray streaking and brown discoloration pattern also align well.

Key evidence:
- Small dark specks visible on the stem surface (microsclerotia) in both the test image and Charcoal Rot references
- Gray/light-colored stem with brown degradation at one end
- The "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance beneath the epidermis is the hallmark diagnostic feature
